selection: Fixed available F26 anchors: first, before midpoint and before final update, in both arms and every seed. No outcome- or gradient-based selection. Reconstruct original training games and batches only; require exact ledger, selected-batch, original metrics/parameter hashes and saved next checkpoints where available.
diagnostic: Measure coefficient-weighted actor/value/entropy gradient geometry on the shared trunk and disjoint heads along the original path. Clone exactly eight updates from original parameters AND original Adam moments, with frozen old likelihoods/advantages/targets and identical minibatch order. Other variants remove only the current shared-trunk value gradient or current entropy gradient. Inherited optimizer history remains; effects are nonadditive and conditional on the frozen batch.
game_signal: Reconstruct selected row to physical-game/seat identities from admitted original selection indices and compare every selected feature/mask/action/log-likelihood/value to original actor records. Report outcomes and advantage variance by stream, physical game and game-seat trajectory. At each original starting checkpoint, four fixed-seed within-stream game partitions compare actor gradients on disjoint physical-game halves. Both seats stay together; halves retain row-weighted means with differing row counts. These overlapping splits are descriptive gradient agreement, not formal SNR or independent replications. No cross-cohort importance-weighted pooling or new trajectories.
interpretation: Exploratory local mechanism audit, no inferential or learning gate. Same-batch surrogate improvement is not out-of-sample policy improvement. Gradient conflict alone does not establish a cause of F26 failure. First establish exact original reproduction; report every anchor and seed. Any subsequent intervention requires a separate full-battle comparison.
